claim: When two sources hold at one boundary, the termination record names the first in the order control stop, t_end, stop requests
fix: The loop checks a pending control stop at frame top, then `t_end`, then the stop requests at each publication. A frame's last publication comes before the next frame top, so a request holding at that boundary is the recorded source even when a control stop is pending or `t_end`'s frame has completed. At a frame top, a control stop is named before `t_end` ([D-203][d-203], [D-268][d-268]).
ver_evidence: Probe: with run!(sim; t_end = 0.3) and a request first holding at 0.3, the source is ModelRequestedStop, not EndTimeReached. With stop!(sim) issued inside frame 3 and a request holding at 0.3, the source is ModelRequestedStop, not ControlRequestedStop(:code). Code: sim.jl:2115/2140 return on the publication's request before the next frame top's checks at sim.jl:2100-2101
ver_note: D-203 (log.md:8101-8103) states the result this sentence copies. D-268 (log.md:11804-11807) and spec §12.4 (10237-10243) apply the order to positions in time instead: requests are read at the publication and the stop word at the next frame top. The code follows that reading for every source, not only for the interrupt. Whether t_end should beat a request at its own boundary needs the user's ruling.

claim: The join timeout already bounds a hook that hangs rather than throws.

ver_evidence: src/sim.jl:1894-1903: _tail! calls unblock!(entry.dev) synchronously on the calling task, before it sets the join deadline. Only the joins run under join_timeout. Probe line 69, with join_timeout = 0.5: a shutdown! that sleeps 3 s returns run! in 0.58 s, but an unblock! that sleeps 3 s holds run! for 3.0 s. A hanging shutdown! is bounded because it runs on the device task inside the wrapper (src/devices.jl:664-667). A hanging unblock! is not bounded.
